title: "Lecture 6 Team Projects"
subtitle: "Bond Portfolio Construction"
---

## Project 1: Build a Practical Bond Index Sample

**Scenario.** Build a transparent sample for a fund that cannot hold every bond in its benchmark.

**Objectives.** Define maturity, sector, quality, and duration cells; select a feasible sample; assess liquidity, turnover, costs, and tracking-error sources.

**Sources.** Public exchange-traded fund (ETF) holdings and fact sheets from the fund sponsor, plus bond trades from [FINRA Fixed Income Data](https://www.finra.org/finra-data/fixed-income). If a complete benchmark cannot be downloaded, use the documented [Lecture 6 fallback portfolio universe and benchmark weights](fallback_data/lecture-6-portfolio.csv).

**Deliverables.** Benchmark table, cells, 10–20 bond sample, exposure gaps, tracking-error budget, and a 10–12 minute presentation.

**Rubric (100 points).** Benchmark diagnosis 20; cell design 25; selection 25; implementation tradeoffs 20; presentation and documentation 10.

## Project 2: Rebalance Under Real-World Constraints

**Scenario.** Bring a drifting portfolio back within limits using no more than five trades.

**Objectives.** Diagnose active duration, sector, issuer, and liquidity exposures; choose trades; include lot sizes, bid-ask costs, and turnover.

**Sources.** Public exchange-traded fund (ETF) holdings, [FINRA Trade Reporting and Compliance Engine (TRACE)](https://www.finra.org/finra-data/fixed-income) observations, and issuer filings from [SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/) or [SEDAR+](https://www.sedarplus.ca/). If live holdings or bid-ask data are incomplete, use the documented [Lecture 6 fallback portfolio, benchmark, and trading-cost snapshot](fallback_data/lecture-6-portfolio.csv).

**Deliverables.** Before/after dashboard, trade list and rationale, transaction-cost estimate, rejected alternatives, and a 10–12 minute presentation.

**Rubric (100 points).** Diagnosis 25; trade design 25; constraints and costs 25; decision quality 15; presentation and reproducibility 10.

## Project 3: Bullet, Barbell, or Ladder?

**Scenario.** Recommend a structure for a five-year income mandate facing uncertain curve changes and annual withdrawals.

**Objectives.** Construct duration-matched bullet, barbell, and ladder portfolios; compare cash-flow timing, convexity, reinvestment risk, liquidity, and behavior under steepening and flattening.

**Sources.** Government terms and yields from [TreasuryDirect](https://www.treasurydirect.gov/auctions/announcements-data-results/) or the [Bank of Canada](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/rates/interest-rates/canadian-bonds/). Use the withdrawal schedule and explicit transaction-cost assumptions in the documented [Lecture 6 fallback portfolio dataset](fallback_data/lecture-6-portfolio.csv) when client inputs are unavailable.

**Deliverables.** Three portfolio tables, cash-flow map, four curve scenarios, tradeoff scorecard, recommendation, and a 10–12 minute presentation.

**Rubric (100 points).** Portfolio construction 25; exposure matching 20; scenarios 25; recommendation 20; presentation and sources 10.

## Project 4: Design an Investment-Grade Mandate

**Scenario.** Translate a nonprofit board's goals into an implementable bond portfolio policy and model allocation.

**Objectives.** Define return objective and risk limits; allocate across government and credit sectors; set duration, quality, issuer, liquidity, and turnover constraints; explain governance and rebalancing.

**Sources.** Public institutional investment policies, broad bond exchange-traded fund (ETF) fact sheets, and yields from [Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/categories/22) or the [Bank of Canada](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/rates/interest-rates/canadian-bonds/). If no suitable client case is available, use the nonprofit mandate and bond universe documented in the [Lecture 6 fallback portfolio dataset](fallback_data/lecture-6-portfolio.csv).

**Deliverables.** One-page policy, strategic allocation, compliance dashboard, two stress tests, implementation plan, and a 10–12 minute presentation.

**Rubric (100 points).** Mandate translation 25; allocation logic 25; constraints 20; stress tests and governance 20; presentation and attribution 10.
